title: One Redis key expired. Then the database died.

sourceReview.learningGoal: Explain cache stampede when a hot key expires, and mitigations: coalesce, lock TTL, jitter, stale-while-revalidate.
sourceReview.caveat: CPU percentages and traffic counts are illustrative storytelling numbers, not a measured production incident. Redis itself did not fail.

claims.claim: Many concurrent misses on the same popular cache key can independently query the database (cache stampede / thundering herd).
Request coalescing or single-flight can share one in-flight regeneration across waiters.
Lock expiry, TTL jitter, and stale-while-revalidate are common mitigations for stampede risk.

beats.headline: Hits stay in Redis.
beats.subhead: Database CPU sits near eight percent.
beats.narration: Five lakh users check the same live cricket score. Every request hits Redis, gets the score, and leaves. Fast. Cheap. Perfect.

beats.headline: One hot key expires.
beats.narration: Then that popular cache key expires. The first request misses Redis. So do the next thousand, and the next ten thousand.

beats.headline: Thousands hit the database.
beats.subhead: CPU goes from calm to fire.
beats.narration: Instead of one rebuild, thousands of requests run straight to the database. CPU goes from calm to one hundred percent.

beats.headline: This is a cache stampede.
beats.subhead: Redis did not crash. Design did.
beats.narration: Redis did not crash. The database did not crash first either. They worked as designed. This failure is called a cache stampede.

beats.headline: Only one rebuild runs.
beats.subhead: Everyone else waits on that result.
beats.narration: Obvious fix: after a miss, let only one request fetch fresh data. Everyone else waits while that request rebuilds the cache.

beats.headline: What if that worker dies?
beats.subhead: Waiters stuck behind a dead lock.
beats.narration: Not quite solved. If that one request crashes while holding the lock, everyone waits for a worker that may never return.

beats.headline: Protect the database.
beats.subhead: Lock TTL, jitter, stale while refresh.
beats.narration: Add lock expiry, TTL jitter, and stale while refresh. Caching is not only speed. It is protecting your database.
